newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish MP resigns ahead of key corruption vote.
newsitem.headline: Turkish MP resigns ahead of key corruption vote.

text.p: A Turkish government MP resigned on Tuesday only hours ahead of a key vote on corruption charges against his party leader and coalition partner Tansu Ciller, Anatolian news agency said.
The agency gave no reason for the resignation of True Path Party deputy Mehmet Korkmaz.
A parliamentary session beginning at 1500 (1300 GMT) will hear accusations that Ciller was involved in graft during her three years as Turkey's first woman prime minister, from 1993.
The resignation brought the number of government deputies to 278. The opposition had been six short of the 276 MPs needed to impeach Ciller but it was not clear what way Korkmaz would vote.
U.S.-educated technocrat Ciller is accused of illegally interfering with the sale of state-owned carmaker TOFAS and failing to prevent graft at the TEDAS electricity company.
Ciller faces a further corruption vote, on the source of her substantial personal wealth, in parliament on Wednesday. The government must also deal with an opposition censure motion next week.
